paragraphs: Ardmore Shipping provides seaborne transportation of petroleum products and chemicals worldwide to oil majors, national oil companies, oil and chemical traders, and chemical companies, with our modern, fuel-efficient fleet of mid-size product and chemical tankers. As of March 6, 2026, our fleet consists of 25 owned vessels and one chartered-in vessel, all of which are in operation.

Ardmore Shipping Corporation was incorporated under the laws of the Republic of the Marshall Islands on May 14, 2013. We commenced business operations through our predecessor company, Ardmore Shipping LLC, on April 15, 2010. On August 6, 2013, we completed our initial public offering of our common stock.

We have 77 wholly owned subsidiaries, a significant number of which represent single ship-owning companies for our fleet, one 50%-owned joint venture entity, Anglo Ardmore Ship Management Limited Pte. Ltd. ("AASML"), which provides technical management services to our fleet, and one 10% equity stake in another entity. A list of our subsidiaries is included as Exhibit 8.1 to this Annual Report.

We maintain our principal executive and management offices at Dorchester House, 7 Church Street, Hamilton, HM11, Bermuda. Our telephone number at these offices is +1 441 292 9332. Ardmore Maritime Services (Asia) Pte. Limited ("AMSA"), a wholly owned subsidiary incorporated in Singapore, carries out our management services and associated functions. Ardmore Shipping Services (Ireland) Limited ("ASSIL"), a wholly owned subsidiary incorporated in Ireland, provides our corporate, accounting, fleet administration, and operations services. Ardmore Shipping (Asia) Pte. Limited ("ASA"), a wholly owned subsidiary incorporated in Singapore, and Ardmore Shipping (Americas) LLC ("ASUSA"), a wholly owned subsidiary incorporated in Delaware, each perform commercial management and chartering services for us.

The SEC's website at www.sec.gov contains reports, proxy statements, and other information regarding issuers that file electronically with the SEC. Our website address is www.ardmoreshipping.com. The information contained on our website is not part of this Annual Report.

We commenced business operations in April 2010 with the goal of building an enduring product and chemical tanker company that emphasizes disciplined capital allocation, service excellence, innovation, and operational efficiency through our focus on high quality, fuel-efficient vessels. We are led by a team of experienced senior managers who have previously held senior management positions with highly regarded shipping companies and financial institutions.

We are strategically focused on modern, fuel-efficient, mid-size product and chemical tankers. We actively pursue opportunities to exploit the overlap we believe exists between the clean petroleum product ("CPP") and chemical sectors in order to enhance earnings, and also seek to engage in more complex CPP trades, such as multi-grade and multi-port loading and discharging operations, where our knowledge of chemical operations is beneficial to our CPP customers.

Our fuel-efficient operations are designed to enhance our operating performance and provide value-added service to our customers. We believe we are at the forefront of fuel efficiency and emissions reduction trends and are well positioned to capitalize on these developments with our fleet of Eco-design vessels. Our acquisition strategy includes to continue to build our fleet with Eco-design newbuildings or Eco-design second-hand vessels and with modern second-hand vessels that can be upgraded to Eco-mod.

We believe that the global energy transition will have a profound impact on the shipping industry, including the product and chemical tanker segments. While this transition will unfold over years, the impact is already being felt through anticipated Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index and Carbon Intensity Indicator regulations and constraints on newbuilding ordering activity.

We are an integrated shipping company. Our fleet is technically managed by a combination of ASSIL and our 50% owned joint venture AASML. We have a resolute focus on both high-quality service and efficient operations, and we believe that our corporate overhead and operating expenses are among the lowest of our peers.

We are commercially independent, as we have no blanket employment arrangements with third-party or related-party commercial managers. Through our in-house chartering and commercial team, we market our services directly to a broad range of customers, including oil majors, national oil companies, oil and chemical traders, chemical companies, and pooling service providers. We monitor the tanker markets to understand how to best utilize our vessels and may change our chartering strategy to take advantage of changing market conditions.
Other than technical management services provided to us by our 50% joint venture AASML we have no related-party transactions concerning our vessel operations or vessel sale and purchase activities.

Certain of our wholly owned subsidiaries carry out our management and administrative services, with AMSA providing us with corporate and executive management services and associated functions, ASSIL providing corporate and accounting administrative services, as well as technical operations services and fleet administration, and ASA, and ASUSA providing our commercial management and chartering services.

In terms of our industry, commodity markets remain subject to heightened levels of uncertainty in connection with the recent U.S., Israel-Iran conflict, and the Russia-Ukraine conflict, which could give rise to regional or broader instability and has resulted in significant economic sanctions against Russia by the U.S., European nations, and other countries which, in turn, could increase uncertainty with respect to global financial markets and production from OPEC and other oil producing nations. Although the Hamas-Israel conflict so far has not had a direct material effect on the tanker industry, since mid-December 2023, Houthi rebels in Yemen have carried out numerous attacks on vessels in the Red Sea area. As a result of these attacks and the conflict in Iran, many shipping companies have routed their vessels away from transiting the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz, which has significantly affected trading patterns, rates and expenses. The U.S. military operations in Venezuela, including the U.S.' recent seizures of certain sanctioned oil tankers calling on Venezuelan ports, has similarly added uncertainty in that region and caused some tankers to re-route or delay voyages. Further escalation, or expansion, of hostilities could continue to affect the price of crude oil and the oil industry, the tanker industry, demand for or services, and our business.

headings: The tanker industry is cyclical and volatile in terms of charter rates and profitability, which may affect our results of operations.
Political instability, terrorist or other attacks, conflict or international hostilities can affect the tanker industry, which may adversely affect our business.
Our insurance may not be adequate to cover our losses that may result from our operations due to the inherent risks of the tanker industry.
Any decrease in spot charter rates in the future or a return of weak spot charter markets may adversely affect our results of operations.
Declines in oil prices may adversely affect our growth prospects and results of operations.
Volatility in the markets in which our vessels trade may result in us having limited liquidity.
Declines in charter rates and other market deterioration could cause us to incur impairment charges.
Interest rate increases could affect the interest rates under our credit facilities and any other potential future variable-rate financing obligations, which could affect our results of operations.
An oversupply of tanker capacity may lead to reductions in charter rates, vessel values, and profitability.
Changes in fuel, or bunkers, prices may adversely affect our results of operations.
Changes in the oil, oil products, and chemical markets could result in decreased demand for our vessels and services.
We operate our vessels worldwide and, as a result, our vessels are exposed to international risks which may reduce revenue or increase expenses.
Acts of piracy on ocean-going vessels could adversely affect our business.
The smuggling of drugs or other contraband onto our vessels may lead to governmental claims against us.
Failure to comply with the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and other anti-corruption laws could result in fines, criminal penalties and an adverse effect on our business.
Developments in safety and environmental requirements relating to the recycling of vessels may result in escalated and unexpected costs.
Maritime claimants could arrest our vessels, which would have a negative effect on our business and results of operations.
Governments could requisition our vessels during a period of conflict or emergency, which may adversely affect our business and results of operations.
Technological innovation could reduce our charter hire income and the value of our vessels.
Public health threats, including pandemics, epidemics and other public health crises, could have an adverse effect on our operations and financial results.
If labor or other interruptions are not resolved in a timely manner, they could have a material adverse effect on our business.
We may not be able to hire or retain qualified seafarers to crew our vessels, which may have an adverse effect on our business and operating results.

We will be required to make substantial capital expenditures to expand the number of vessels in our fleet and to maintain all our vessels, which will depend on our ability to obtain additional financing.

paragraphs: Some of the risks summarized below and discussed in greater detail in the following pages relate principally to the industry in which we operate and to our business in general. Other risks relate principally to the securities market and to ownership of our securities. The occurrence of any of the events described in this section could significantly and negatively affect our business, financial condition, operating results, and ability to pay dividends on our shares of common stock, or the trading price of our shares of common stock.
● The tanker industry is cyclical and volatile in terms of charter rates and profitability.
● Political instability, terrorist or other attacks, conflict or international hostilities can affect the tanker industry.
● Failure to protect our information systems against cyberattacks, security breaches or system failure could adversely affect our business and results of operations.
● We are subject to certain risks with respect to our counterparties on contracts.

● The state of global financial markets and economic conditions may adversely impact our ability to obtain additional financing or to refinance existing financing or otherwise negatively impact our business.

paragraphs: During the second quarter of 2025, we agreed to acquire three modern, high-quality, Korean-built MR tankers in two separate transactions: one 2020-built scrubber-installed vessel for $38.3 million and two 2017-built vessels for $32.8 million each, for an aggregate purchase price of $103.9 million. We took delivery of all three vessels during the third quarter of 2025. This transaction was financed by cash on hand and borrowings under revolving credit facilities, maintaining a modest leverage level while lowering average fleet age.

While we primarily trade our fleet in the spot market, we enhanced our fixed-coverage during the year ended December 31, 2025, with top-tier oil majors and a leading chemical producer. In total, we currently have four MR tankers employed on time charter at an average rate of $22,650 per day, and one chemical tanker on a three-year time charter at $19,250 per day – bringing our fixed-rate coverage to five vessels.

In July 2025, we closed a $350 million revolving credit facility on favorable terms, secured by 20 of our owned vessels. The facility is priced at SOFR plus a margin of 1.80% and matures in 2031. The bank group in the revolving credit facility is comprised of Nordea Bank, Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken AB (publ), ABN AMRO Bank, and Danske Bank A/S.

paragraphs: Ardmore Shipping 提供石油產品與化學品的國際海上運輸服務，服務對象包括油公司、國家油公司、油與化學品貿易商以及化學公司，我們擁有現代化、節能的中型產品與化學品油輪船隊。截至 2026 年 3 月 6 日，我們的船隊包含 25 艘自有船舶與 1 艘租入船舶，所有船舶皆處於運作狀態。
Ardmore Shipping Corporation 於 2013 年 5 月 14 日根據馬紹爾羣島共和國法律設立。我們透過前身公司 Ardmore Shipping LLC 於 2010 年 4 月 15 日開始營運。我們於 2013 年 8 月 6 日完成首次公開發行普通股。
我們擁有 77 家 wholly owned 子公司，其中許多為單一船舶所有公司，用以支撐我們的船隊，一家 50% 股權的合資企業 Anglo Ardmore Ship Management Limited Pte. Ltd. ("AASML")，提供技術管理服務給我們的船隊，以及一家 10% 股權的其他企業。我們的子公司名單載於本年度報告的附錄 8.1。

我們的總部與管理辦公室設於 Bermuda 的 Hamilton, HM11, Dorchester House, 7 Church Street。這些辦公室的電話號碼為 +1 441 292 9332。Ardmore Maritime Services (Asia) Pte. Limited ("AMSA")，一家在新加坡設立的 wholly owned 子公司，執行我們的管理服務與相關功能。Ardmore Shipping Services (Ireland) Limited ("ASSIL")，一家在愛爾蘭設立的 wholly owned 子公司，提供我們的企業、會計、船隊管理與運作服務。Ardmore Shipping (Asia) Pte. Limited ("ASA")，一家在新加坡設立的 wholly owned 子公司，以及 Ardmore Shipping (Americas) LLC ("ASUSA")，一家在 Delaware 設立的 wholly owned 子公司，各自為我們執行商業管理與租賃服務。
美國證券交易委員會 (SEC) 的網站 www.sec.gov 提供報告、股東信函與其他有關向 SEC 提交電子檔發行人的資訊。我們的網站地址為 www.ardmoreshipping.com。本網站的資訊並非本年度報告的一部分。
我們於 2010 年 4 月開始營運，目標是建立一家持續經營的產品與化學品油輪公司，強調嚴謹的資本配置、服務卓越、創新與運作效率，透過我們對高品質、節能船舶的專注。我們由一羣經驗豐富的高階管理團隊領導，這些管理人員曾擔任知名運輸公司與金融機構的高階管理職位。
我們戰略上專注於現代化、節能、中型產品與化學品油輪。我們積極尋求機會利用我們相信在潔淨石油產品 ("CPP") 與化學品部門之間存在的重疊，以提高獲利，同時也尋求參與更複雜的 CPP 貿易，例如多級別與多港口裝卸作業，我們在化學品運作方面的知識對 CPP 客戶有幫助。
我們的節能運作旨在提升運營表現並為客戶提供附加價值的服務。我們相信我們在節能與減排趨勢方面處於領先地位，並以我們的 Eco-design 船隊，有優勢可抓住這些發展。我們的收購策略包括持續以 Eco-design 新造船或 Eco-design 二手船，以及現代二手船建造船隊，這些船隻可升級為 Eco-mod。
我們認為全球能源轉型將對造船業產生深遠影響，包括散裝貨船與化學品運輸船等子類別。雖然此轉型過程將持續多年，但其影響已透過預期的能源效率現有船舶指數與碳強度指標規範及新造船訂單活動的限制而開始體現。
我們是一家整合型造船公司。我們的船隊由 ASSIL 與我們 50% 股權的合資公司 AASML 共同技術管理。我們致力於提供高品質服務與高效運作，並相信我們的企業營運費用與營運費用在業內屬於最低水準之一。
我們在商業上具有獨立性，因為我們與第三方或關聯企業的商業經理並無總體僱用協議。透過我們內設的租賃與商業團隊，我們直接向廣泛的客戶羣銷售服務，包括石油大廠、國家石油公司、石油與化學品貿易商、化學品公司與池化服務供應商。我們監測貨船市場，以瞭解如何最佳化利用我們的船舶，並可能根據市場變動調整我們的租賃策略。
除了由我們 50% 合資公司 AASML 提供的技術管理服務外，我們與船舶運作或船舶買賣活動無關聯交易。
部分我們的 wholly owned 子公司執行我們的管理與行政服務，AMSA 為我們提供企業與高階管理服務及相關功能，ASSIL 提供企業與會計行政服務，以及技術運作服務與船隊管理，ASA 與 ASUSA 則提供我們的商業管理與租賃服務。

就我們所屬的產業而言，商品市場仍因近期美國、以色列與伊朗衝突，以及俄羅斯與烏克蘭衝突而面臨更高程度的不確定性，這可能導致區域或更廣泛的不穩定，並已導致美國、歐洲國家及其他國家對俄羅斯實施重大經濟制裁，進而可能增加全球金融市場與 OPEC 及其他石油生產國產能的不確定性。儘管哈瑪斯與以色列衝突迄今尚未對貨船產業產生重大影響，但自 2023 年 12 月中以來，也門的胡賽叛軍已對紅海區域的船舶進行多次攻擊。由於這些攻擊與伊朗的衝突，許多造船公司已將其船舶航線遠離紅海與霍爾木茲 Strait，這已顯著影響交易模式、價格與費用。美國在委內瑞拉的軍事行動，包括美國近期扣押某些被制裁的油輪，這些油輪停靠委內瑞拉港口，也已使該地區增加不確定性，並導致部分油輪重新規劃航線或延遲航程。進一步升級或擴大衝突，可能持續影響原油價格與石油產業、貨船產業、需求或服務，以及我們的業務。

paragraphs: 於 2025 年第二季，本公司同意以兩筆交易取得三艘現代化、高品質、韓國建造的 MR 油輪：一艘 2020 年建造並裝設 scrubber 的船舶，價格為 38.3 百萬美元；以及兩艘 2017 年建造的船舶，每艘價格為 32.8 百萬美元，總計購入價格為 103.9 百萬美元。本公司於 2025 年第三季完成所有三艘船舶的交付。此交易由現金及循環信用融資資金融資，維持適度的負債水平，同時降低船隊平均年齡。
雖然本公司主要在現貨市場交易船隊，但在 2025 年截至 12 月 31 日的會計年度中，我們加強了固定覆蓋率，與頂級油公司及一家領先的化學品生產商合作。目前，本公司共有四艘 MR 油輪以日租形式租賃，平均每日租金為 22,650 美元，以及一艘化學品油輪以三年期日租形式租賃，每日租金為 19,250 美元 – 使固定利率覆蓋率達到五艘船舶。

於 2025 年 7 月，本公司完成了一筆 350 百萬美元的循環信用融資設施，條件優良，以本公司所有 20 艘船舶作為擔保。該設施的利率為 SOFR 加上 1.80% 的幅度，並於 2031 年到期。循環信用融資設施的銀行羣體包括 Nordea Bank、Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken AB (publ)、ABN AMRO Bank 以及 Danske Bank A/S。

headings: 油輪產業具有週期性且在租賃率與獲利能力方面表現波動，這可能會影響我們的營運結果。
政治動盪、恐怖攻擊或其他攻擊、衝突或國際敵對行動可能影響油輪產業，這可能會對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們的保險可能無法充分覆蓋因營運所導致的損失，這是因為油輪產業本身具有內在風險。
未來租賃率下降或-spot charter 市場再度走弱，可能會對我們的營運結果產生不利影響。
原油價格下跌可能對我們的成長前景及營運結果產生不利影響。
我們船舶交易市場的波動性可能導致我們擁有有限的流動性。
租賃費率下降及其他市場惡化情況可能導致本公司需提列減損費用。
利率上升可能影響本公司信用融資協議下的利率及任何其他潛在未來變動利率融資義務，這可能會影響本公司營運成果。
油輪供應過度可能導致租賃費率、船舶價值及利潤減少。
燃料或 bunkers 價格變動可能不利影響本公司營運成果。
石油、石油產品及化學品市場變動可能導致本公司船舶及服務需求減少。
本公司在全球範圍內運營船舶，因此本公司船舶面臨國際風險，這可能會降低收入或增加費用。
對海上船舶的劫掠行為可能不利影響本公司業務。
毒品或其他違禁品被走私至本公司船舶上，可能導致政府對本公司提出索賠。
